title: Staged pager gating with proportional impact scoring to reduce SLO noise
creator: Priya Raman
description: Summary: After the March 2026 capacity regression incident we observed a cascade of burn-rate pages where low-impact spikes in a small set of tenants triggered global burn alerts and noisy oncall rotations. This ticket proposes a staging gate for pager escalation that combines a short inertia window, proportional impact scoring by tenant and route, and a severity-decay policy so the pager surface only escalates for sustained, impactful problems. Goal: reduce false and low-value pages by at least 60% for burn-rate-derived SLO alerts without increasing time-to-detect for high-impact regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume from burn-rate SLOs decreased by >=60% on average for non-severity incidents over a 14-day trial window
No increase in mean time to detect (MTTD) for incidents with customer_impact=high; measure via alert-to-ack median
Stakeholders (SRE, runtime, product) sign-off on escalation thresholds and the proportionate scoring formula
Runbook updated with new staged-gating flow and rollback steps
A/B trial completed on 2 regions (us-west1, eu-central) and telemetry dashboards validated
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Design: define proportional impact score components (tenant token volume, route error rate, p99 latency delta, recent prefix cache miss rate)
Phase 2 - Prototype: implement inertial open window (30s sliding) + additive impact scoring in alerting pipeline; route to muted-signal channel instead of pager when score < threshold
Phase 3 - Canary: enable staged gating for non-prod and 10% traffic in us-west1 for 72h, collect false-positive metrics and adjust weights
Phase 4 - Gradual rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% across regions with monitoring and automated rollback on regression
Phase 5 - Post-rollout: run a 14-day effectiveness report and fold thresholds into runtime-1.21 release notes
engineering_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE, runtime, and product. Agreed to try a short inertia window (30s) and tenant-weighted impact scoring as primary lever.
2026-03-04: Prototype implemented in alert-bridge service; staged alerts now land in #slo-staging instead of paging for low-score events.

2026-03-06: Observed initial reduction in paging by ~42% for staged set; noticed edge-case where multi-tenant simultaneous small spikes still aggregated to high score — added route-level damping factor.
2026-03-09: Canary rollout started in us-west1 on 10% traffic. Telemetry integration added to console: 'staged-pager' tag and impact score histogram.
2026-03-10: Collected first 48h metrics from canary; false-positive pages down 63% in canary cohort. Preparing A/B plan for eu-central next week.
comments: SRE Lead (Dana Cole) 2026-03-03: prefer 30s inertia but want explicit override flag for ongoing incidents. Action: add incident_override boolean to the gating logic.
Product (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-04: confirm customer-visible alerting SLA remains unchanged for P0/P1 customers. Action: ensure tier-aware thresholds.
Runtime (Mei Chen) 2026-03-06: suggested including 'prefixed-kv-cache-miss' as a factor; implemented route-level damping to prevent cross-tenant aggregation.
Oncall (Aaron Blake) 2026-03-09: initial canary behaved well; request simple dashboard visible in Console top nav for the next rollout step.
